events.title: Edgar Allan Poe is born in Boston
events.description: The future poet and writer was born in Boston, Massachusetts. He became a master of macabre tales and haunting verse, and is widely credited with helping to shape the modern detective story.
events.significance: Poe's work shaped American literature, detective fiction and the horror genre, and it still influences writers and filmmakers.

events.title: Georgia secedes from the Union
events.description: Georgia became the fifth state to vote to leave the United States. It followed South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi and Alabama.
events.significance: Georgia's secession added to the momentum that led to the Confederacy and the outbreak of the American Civil War.

events.title: Zeppelins bomb Britain for the first time
events.description: German Zeppelin airships carried out the first major raid of their bombing campaign against Britain. They attacked several towns in Norfolk, including Great Yarmouth.
events.significance: The raid opened a new chapter in warfare by bringing strategic aerial bombing to civilian populations.

events.title: Indira Gandhi becomes India's first female prime minister
events.description: Indira Gandhi was chosen to lead India's government after the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri. She became the country's first woman to hold the office.
events.significance: She led India for most of the next two decades and became one of the most influential and debated figures in modern world politics.

events.title: Apple announces the Lisa computer
events.description: Apple unveiled the Lisa, its first commercial personal computer with a graphical user interface and a mouse.
events.significance: Lisa was a commercial disappointment, but it helped popularize the point-and-click interface that shaped later personal computers.
